title: The Crab Derby, 2019
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Thirty-fifth annual. Gully's girl, nine, draws it from a photo of a real crab. It's good. It's not a cartoon. Wood letters and says nothing about that.

panels.composition: Gully's. The girl, nine, drawing from a photo on Gully's phone propped against the register. Careful. Eight legs, the joints right. WOOD watching, not lettering yet.

image.prompt: a nine-year-old girl carefully drawing a crab from a photo on a phone propped against a shop register, a thin man watching without interrupting, a man in an apron, a dog, clean ink

panels.composition: Her crab. Accurate. Shaded. The strip draws it better than the strip's own crabs, deliberately.

image.prompt: close-up of a child's careful pencil drawing of a crab with correct joints and shading, better than a cartoon

panels.composition: Wood lettering under it. His hand steady. His face doing something he doesn't let it finish.

image.prompt: a man lettering beneath a child's drawing with a steady hand and an expression he holds back

panels.composition: Twenty-two flyers. The twenty-second is the best one on the wall. Gully looking at Wood, not the flyer.

image.prompt: a row of twenty-two crab flyers on a shingle wall where the newest is plainly the best, a man in an apron looking not at the wall but at his friend, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: Her crab is the best one on the wall. Gully looks at Wood, not the flyer.
